links.outcome: Self-reported anxiety, depression, stress, angst, craving with ML-alert-triggered PRSS calls vs standard care
links.effect: PRSS arm (n=26) had modest but significant decreases in anxiety, stress, depression, angst composite (all p<0.001) and maximum craving (p=0.011) vs SoC (n=37); drug use recurrence not measured.
links.quote: Statistically significant reductions were noted in anxiety, depression, stress, angst, and cravings in the PRSS intervention arm relative to the SoC arm, though the extent of the differences was modest, therefore likely tempering the clinical significance.

links.outcome: Staff burden from responding to algorithm-generated alerts
links.effect: PRSS made 483 call attempts, ~20 per participant (range 1-53), ~21 calls/week; only 36% of first calls answered; burden on PRSS described as high.
links.quote: Important aspects related to feasibility included difficulties with learning how to use the RNI Health app, the high burden of daily entries with the RNI Health app, limited battery life of the wearable devices, loss of wearable devices, and the high burden of responding by phone to numerous alerts generated by the algorithms.

links.outcome: Anxiety, depression, stress, angst composite, and maximum craving following alert-linked peer outreach
links.effect: Adding PRSS calls to participant alerts modestly reduced anxiety, stress, depression, and angst composite (all p's < 0.001) and maximum craving (p = 0.011). Calls included random as well as anomaly-triggered alerts.
links.quote: Statistically significant reductions were noted in anxiety, depression, stress, angst, and cravings in the PRSS intervention arm relative to the SoC arm, though the extent of the differences was modest, therefore likely tempering the clinical significance.

links.outcome: Data-collection compliance and participant and staff workflow burden
links.effect: Across 229 participants, compliance declined from ∼41 days during Baseline to ∼30 days during Phase 1 to ∼21 days during Phase 2; daily entries and alert-response calls were burdensome.
links.quote: Important aspects related to feasibility included difficulties with learning how to use the RNI Health app, the high burden of daily entries with the RNI Health app, limited battery life of the wearable devices, loss of wearable devices, and the high burden of responding by phone to numerous alerts generated by the algorithms.

screen.practice: human peer support follow-up triggered by ML anomaly alerts
screen.reason: The study evaluated a prospective randomized trial where machine learning anomaly detection triggered alerts directly to participants and escalated alerts to peer recovery support specialists (PRSS), comparing outcomes against standard care.

primary.practice: peer recovery support specialist escalation/intervention upon alert
